population: Iranian; Birjand Longitudinal Aging Study (BLAS), ages 60-90
conclusion: Two analyses, both null. (1) LONGEVITY, the estimate this row carries: cross-sectional allele frequency across three age bands - T allele 1.39% at 60-69, 4.65% at 70-79, 0% at 80-90 (0 of 80 alleles); Fisher's exact p = 0.073 across bands, p = 0.06 for 70-79 vs 80-90. (2) FRAILTY, the study's own primary hypothesis, not supported: unadjusted allelic OR 1.4, p = 0.36; final multivariable logistic model adjusted for age, sex, smoking, physical activity, nutritional status, BMI, hypertension and congestive heart failure gave OR 0.96, 95% CI 0.10-9.66, p = 0.98. Only 8 heterozygotes and no T/T homozygote were seen in 227 people, and no date-of-death data was available, so neither analysis could test survival directly. Both intervals span an order of magnitude either side of 1: uninformative nulls, not demonstrated absence of effect. (Only one row per paper is permitted here, so the frailty estimate is recorded in this prose rather than as its own row.)
study_design: case-control nested in a prospective cohort (frail n=39, pre-frail n=150, robust n=38), plus cross-sectional allele frequency across age bands
statistical_test: Fisher's exact test (allelic) across three age bands, unadjusted; frailty also by multiple logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, smoking, physical activity, nutritional status (MNA), BMI, hypertension and congestive heart failure
provenance_quote: the frequency of the T allele was numerically lower in the 80–90 years age group (0%) compared to the 60–69 (1.39%) and 70–79 (4.65%) age groups

population: Finnish men; Helsinki Birth Cohort Study + Helsinki Businessmen Study
conclusion: The study that first reported this variant, and the source the 2025 paper builds on. Longer-living healthy men (43 from HBCS plus 63 from HBS of mean age 83) compared with 92 men who had died of natural causes at mean age 66.6. T allele in 1/43 HBCS long-lived (MAF 0.012) and 2/63 HBS (MAF 0.016) versus 9/92 controls (MAF 0.049). Combined two-tailed Fisher's exact OR 3.58, 95% CI 0.96-13.4, p = 0.074 for the T allele in the shorter-lived group; the HBCS-only estimate was OR 4.37, 95% CI 0.54-35.1, p = 0.18. Genotypes in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Male-only by design, and the authors state 427 cases and 371 controls would be needed for 80% power - so this is roughly a quarter of the sample its own authors called adequate. This paper describes the variant as an INTRON VARIANT in both of its tables; see README.
study_design: extreme-phenotype case-control, two Finnish cohorts combined, male only
statistical_test: two-tailed Fisher's exact test (allelic), combined cohorts, unadjusted
provenance_quote: The p-value of two-tailed Fisher exact test performed for these was 0.07 whereas OR was 3.58
